sections.shortTitle: Unani Ayurvedic and Homeopathic Practitioners Amendment Ordinance 1997
sections.description:
Short title and commencement

ORDINANCE XXVIII OF 1997
ORDINANCE XXVIII OF 1997
UNANI, AYURVEDIC AND HOMEOPATHIC
PRACTITIONERS (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1997
An Ordinance further to amend the
Unanai, Ayurvedic and Homeopathic
Practitioners Act, 1965
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary,
Part I, 13th February, 1997]
No. F.2(1)‑97‑Pub.‑‑dated
13‑2‑1997. The following Ordinance made by the President is hereby
published for general information:‑‑
Whereas it is expedient further to
amend the Unani, Ayurvedic and Homeopathic Practitioners Act, 1965 (II of
1965), for the purposes hereinafter.
And Whereas the National Assembly is
not in session and the President is satisfied that the circumstances exist
which render it necessary to take immediate action.
Now, therefore in exercise of the
powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
1. Short title and commencement.‑‑(1) This Ordinance may
be called the Unani, Ayurvedic and Homeopathic Practitioners (Amendment)
Ordinance, 1997.
(2) It shall come into force at
once.
1. Amendment of section 13, Act II
of 1965.‑‑In
the Unani, Ayurvedic and Homeopathic Practitioners, 1965 (II of 1965),
hereinafter referred to as the said Act, the existing section 13 shall be
numbered as sub‑section (1) of that section and after subsection (1),
numbered as aforesaid, the following new sub section shall be added, namely:‑‑
"(2) If at any time it appears
to the Federal Government that any member of the Council has failed to exercise
or has exceeded or abused any power conferred upon him under this Act, it may,
if satisfied that such failure, excess or abuse has adversely affected the
efficient conduct of such member in achieving the objectives of this act and after
giving him an opportunity of showing cause against the action proposed to be
taken, by notification in the official gazette, disqualify him from the
membership of the Council."

substituted, namely:‑‑
"(4) After considering the
report of the such local inquiry, if any, and making such further inquiry as
may appear to it to be necessary, the Council shall forward the application

recognition may be subject to such terms and conditions, if any, as may be

6. Amendment of section 24, Act II
of 1965.‑‑In
the said Act, in section 24, after subsection (2), the following new
subsections shall be added, namely:‑‑
"(3) Subject to the provisions
of this Act, the registration of a practitioner under this Act shall be valid
until the 31st day of December of the year next following the year in which it
is made and shall thereafter be renewable for a period of five years on the
application of the practitioner accompanied by the prescribed fee:
Provided that the registration of a
practitioner made at any time before the 31st day of December 1996, shall
continue to be valid until the 31st day of December, 1997.
(4) Subject to the provisions of
this Act, the enlistment of a practitioner on the list shall be valid until
31st day of December, 1997, and shall thereafter be renewable for a period of
five years on the application of the practitioner accompanied by the prescribed
fee. "
